43.s: What is true about Censure Motion?
o: It is not different from No-confidence motion
It is different from the No-confidence motion
It is not mandatory to mention the reasons in this
Permission of the House is not essential to present it
43.x: and (d) There is a clear difference between a Censure Motion and a No-Confidence Motion in terms of purpose and procedure. In a Censure Motion, a clear mention of reasons is mandatory. For a Censure Motion, separate “leave of the House” is not required. Factually, both (b) and (d) are correct. That is why the Bihar Public Service Commission removed (deleted) this question from evaluation.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about privilege, no-confidence and censure motions:
1. A privilege motion is raised in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha under Rule 198 and Rule 167 respectively.
2. The first no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers was moved against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963 by J.B. Kripalani.
3. Passing a Censure Motion does not compel the Council of Ministers to resign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: a privilege motion is governed by Rule 222 (Lok Sabha) and Rule 187 (Rajya Sabha); Rule 198 (LS) is the no-confidence motion.
Statement 2: Correct: the first no-confidence motion against Nehru was moved in 1963 by J.B. Kripalani.
Statement 3: Correct: a passed Censure Motion does not compel resignation; a passed No-confidence Motion does.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary motions and resolutions:
1. A resolution moved under a constitutional or statutory provision is called a substitute motion.
2. A motion raised against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts is a Privilege Motion.
3. If a Confidence Motion moved by the Government is defeated in the Lok Sabha, the Government falls.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: such a resolution is a statutory resolution, not a substitute motion.
Statement 2: Correct: a privilege motion targets a Minister who withheld or distorted facts.
Statement 3: Correct: defeat of a confidence motion shows the Government has lost the Lok Sabha's support, so it falls.

43.s: Which of the following statements regarding confidence and no-confidence motions is incorrect?
o: A Confidence Motion demonstrates the Government's majority.
A No-Confidence Motion is moved by the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
A No-Confidence Motion is moved by the Council of Ministers to demonstrate its majority.
A Confidence Motion is moved on the floor by the Council of Ministers or the Government.
43.x: C is incorrect: a confidence motion is moved by the government to prove its majority; a no-confidence motion is moved by the Opposition (Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha).
n: A Confidence Motion is moved on the floor by the Council of Ministers or the Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
A Confidence Motion demonstrates the majority of the Council of Ministers or Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
A No-Confidence Motion is moved by the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
xs: The incorrect statement is that a **No-Confidence Motion is moved by the Council of Ministers** to demonstrate its majority — option **(3)**.
A **No-Confidence Motion** (**Rule 198**) is moved by the **Opposition** in the **Lok Sabha**.
A **Confidence Motion** is moved by the **Government** (Council of Ministers) to **demonstrate its majority**.
xa: If a confidence motion is defeated, the **Government falls**.
The no-confidence motion needs **50** members' support; **no reasons** need be stated.
First no-confidence motion: **J.B. Kripalani**, **1963**, against **Nehru**.

43.s: Which of the following statements about a Privilege Motion is incorrect?
o: It automatically forces the Government to resign.
It may be raised against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts.
It requires the consent of the Presiding Officer.
It is admissible in either House of Parliament.
43.x: Option A is incorrect: a privilege motion does not make the government resign. It is raised against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts, needs the presiding officer's consent and goes to the Committee of Privileges.
43.tq: Discriminate the motions that bring down a government from the others.
n: A Privilege Motion is raised against a Minister for withholding facts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion is raised against a Minister for distorting facts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion is admissible in either House of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion requires the consent of the Presiding Officer. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xs: The incorrect statement is that a privilege motion **automatically forces the Government to resign** — option **(1)**.
It is raised against a **Minister** for **withholding or distorting facts**.
It is admissible in **either House**, with the **Presiding Officer's** consent, and referred to the **Committee of Privileges**.
xa: Committee of Privileges: **15 members** (LS, nominated by the **Speaker**); **10** (RS, by the **Chairman**).
Only a passed **no-confidence motion** makes the Council resign.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about Rule 184 of the Lok Sabha:
1. It permits a discussion on a matter of public interest followed by a formal motion and voting.
2. Defeat of a motion under Rule 184 can threaten the ruling party.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: Rule 184 allows a discussion ending in a formal motion and vote, and defeat on that vote can threaten the ruling party.
n: Rule 184 of the Lok Sabha permits discussion on a matter of public interest accompanied by a formal motion and voting. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
If a Rule 184 motion is defeated, the ruling party faces potential collapse. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: Rule 184 is a **substantive** motion with significant political consequences.
**Rule 193:** short-duration discussion, **no voting**.
**Half-an-hour discussion:** no formal motion or vote.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about a no-confidence motion:
1. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. It requires the support of 50 members.
3. Reasons must be stated while moving it.
Which of the above statements are correct?
43.x: A no-confidence motion (Rule 198) is moved only in the Lok Sabha with the support of 50 members; it needs no reasons, unlike a censure motion.
n: A No-Confidence Motion is moved only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Rule 198 governs a No-Confidence Motion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
A No-Confidence Motion requires the support of 50 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
A No-Confidence Motion requires no reasons to be stated. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xa: It is against the **entire Council of Ministers**, not an individual minister.
First moved by **J.B. Kripalani** in **1963**.
Andhra State: **Gouthu Latchanna's** motion (Nov **1954**) — **69 for, 68 against**.

43.s: Which motion must state specific reasons for its adoption?
43.x: A censure motion must state reasons; a no-confidence motion needs 50 members' support but no reasons, and the government moves a confidence motion.
n: A No-Confidence Motion requires the support of 50 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
A Confidence Motion is moved by the Council of Ministers or the Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Specific reasons must be stated for a Censure Motion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
A Calling Attention motion does not contain an element of censure or condemnation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xa: Censure may be against an **individual minister** or the **entire Council**.
A passed censure motion does **not** force resignation.
No-confidence passed → Council **must resign**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about State Legislatures:
1. They use the same devices as Parliament, such as Question Hour and motions, to control the executive.
2. They also use estimates and public accounts committees for this purpose.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: State Legislatures use the same parliamentary devices for executive control and also use estimates and public accounts committees.
xa: The Union tools: Question Hour, Zero Hour, half-an-hour and short-duration discussions, and **calling attention**, **adjournment**, **censure** and **no-confidence** motions.
Committees: **Government Assurances**, **Petitions**, **Subordinate Legislation**, **PAC**, **Estimates**; plus **Budget approval** and the **Motion of Thanks**.
The **AP Legislature** uses the same devices — e.g., the AP Legislative Council was adjourned amid a Question Hour row on the **Tirumala laddu** issue (**Feb 2026**).

43.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:
1. The President appoints the Chairpersons of all Department-related Standing Committees.
2. A Minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
3. The Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) was created on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: the Speaker appoints the Chairpersons of Lok Sabha DRSCs and the Chairman those of Rajya Sabha DRSCs, not the President.
Statement 2: Correct: Ministers cannot be members of the Public Accounts Committee.
Statement 3: Correct: COPU came from the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about financial committees and legislatures:
1. The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921.
2. The Estimates Committee is described as the "Continuous economy committee".
3. Biometric attendance for MLAs in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was introduced from the Budget Session of 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
Statement 2: Correct: the Estimates Committee is known as the "Continuous economy committee."
Statement 3: Correct: Andhra Pradesh introduced biometric attendance for MLAs from its Budget Session in 2026.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about financial committees of Parliament:
1. The Estimates Committee, with 30 members drawn from the Lok Sabha only, is the largest parliamentary committee.
2. Ministers are barred from the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Petitions mainly because these committees meet only when Parliament is not in session.
3. Since 1967, the Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings has been appointed from the Opposition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the Estimates Committee is the largest, with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.
Statement 2: Incorrect: Ministers are kept out because these committees scrutinise the government.
Statement 3: Incorrect: since 1967 the Speaker has appointed the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, not COPU, from the Opposition.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the three Financial Committees of Parliament:
1. Their members are elected by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
2. Each has a tenure of one year.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: Members of the PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings Committees are elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote, for one year.
n: Members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Members of the Estimates Committee are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Members of the Committee on Public Undertakings are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The tenure of the Public Accounts Committee is one year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The tenure of the Estimates Committee is one year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The tenure of the Committee on Public Undertakings is one year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: **Ministers cannot** be members of any of the three.
PAC recommendations are **not binding**.

43.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Estimates Committee – examination of budget estimates
Public Accounts Committee – scrutiny of public-sector undertaking accounts and commercial soundness
Estimates Committee – suggesting economy in administration
Committee on Public Undertakings – scrutiny of PSU accounts
43.x: The PAC scrutinises appropriation accounts and wasteful expenditure; PSU accounts are examined by the Committee on Public Undertakings.
n: The Public Accounts Committee scrutinizes appropriation accounts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Public Accounts Committee scrutinizes wasteful expenditure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Estimates Committee examines budget estimates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Estimates Committee suggests economy in administration. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Estimates Committee suggests administrative efficiency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Public Undertakings scrutinizes public-sector undertaking accounts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Public Undertakings scrutinizes commercial soundness. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: The PAC examines **execution**, not policy.
PAC was set up in **1921**; CPU in **1964**.
"Examines CAG reports" = **PAC** (and **CPU** for PSUs).

43.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees and resolutions:
1. After a resolution has been moved in Parliament, a resolution on the same subject is barred for one year.
2. The Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions maintains close contact with the Chief Whips of political parties in both Houses of Parliament.
3. Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were set up in 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: a resolution on the same subject is barred for one year.
Statement 2: Incorrect: it is the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs who keeps close contact with the Chief Whips.
Statement 3: Correct: DRSCs were set up in 1993; there are 24, each with 31 members.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary committees:
1. Ad hoc committees of Parliament do not continue permanently after completing their assigned task.
2. Committees such as the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are described as ad hoc committees.
3. The Committee on Government Assurances is described as the 'Ombudsman' of Parliament, examining petitions on bills and on matters of general public interest.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: ad hoc committees end when their assigned task is completed.
Statement 2: Incorrect: these committees are described as watchdogs over the executive, not ad hoc committees.
Statement 3: Incorrect: the Committee on Petitions is Parliament's 'Ombudsman'; the Committee on Government Assurances tracks ministers' promises.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:
1. No minister can be a member of the Committee.
2. A minister may become a member if nominated by the Speaker.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: No minister can be a member of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
xa: It has **30 members** = **20 from Lok Sabha + 10 from Rajya Sabha**.
**Committee on Empowerment of Women**: both Houses, constituted **29 April 1997**.
**PAC** and **Estimates Committee** also bar ministers.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about committees and reform bodies:
1. The Shanta Kumar Committee's recommendations are associated with a code of ethics, the Right to Public Services and e-governance.
2. In the 17th Lok Sabha, 16% of Bills were referred to parliamentary committees.
3. The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first constituted as an ad-hoc committee in 2000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Incorrect: these are linked with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission; Shanta Kumar dealt with FCI/PDS.
Statement 2: Correct: only 16% of Bills in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees, against 71% in the 15th.
Statement 3: Correct: it was first set up as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000 and made permanent in 2015.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee:
1. It can take up matters that are sub-judice.
2. It was made a permanent committee in 2015.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: The Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015, but it cannot take up matters pending in court.
n: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee became permanent in 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee cannot take up sub-judice matters. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: It was first constituted as an **Ad-hoc Committee** on **16 May 2000**.
It oversees the **moral and ethical conduct** of members.
**Rajya Sabha** Ethics Committee: constituted **4 March 1997**.

43.s: Which of the following statements about the Committee on Petitions is incorrect?
o: The Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions has 15 members.
Ministers may be elected or nominated as members of the Committee on Petitions.
It examines petitions and representations submitted to the House.
The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions has 10 members.
43.x: Option B is incorrect: Ministers cannot be members of the Petitions Committee. It has 15 members in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
43.tq: Remember that scrutiny committees exclude Ministers.
n: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions submitted to the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Petitions examines representations submitted to the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions has 15 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions has 10 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Ministers cannot be members of the Committee on Petitions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **Ministers may be elected or nominated** to the Committee on Petitions — option **(2)**.
**Ministers cannot** be members of the Committee on Petitions.
It has **15** members in the **Lok Sabha** and **10** in the **Rajya Sabha**, and examines **petitions and representations**.
xa: It is called the **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament.
Ministers are also barred from the **PAC**, **Estimates Committee**, **CPU** and **Subordinate Legislation** committee.
It examines petitions on **bills** and matters of **public interest**.

43.s:
Assertion (A): The gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months.
Reason (R): Article 85 implies that Parliament must have at least two sessions in a year.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
43.x: Both are true: Article 85 bars a gap of more than six months between sessions, and so Parliament must meet at least twice a year. R is a consequence of A, not its explanation.
43.tq: Check the direction of cause and consequence.
n: The maximum gap between Parliamentary sessions is six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Article 85 provides for the maximum six-month gap between Parliamentary sessions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The six-month maximum session gap implies a minimum of two Parliamentary sessions per year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
xs: **Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation** of A — option **(2)**.
A: the **maximum gap** between two sessions is **six months** — **Article 85**.
R: this **implies** a **minimum** of **two** sessions **per year** — a consequence of A, not its cause.
xa: **Quorum:** **one-tenth** of the total membership — **Article 100**.
The Lok Sabha can list a **maximum** of **20 oral starred questions** per day.
The **Budget, Monsoon and Winter** sessions are by convention.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary discussions, whips and the PAC:
1. A half-an-hour discussion in Parliament is held on a matter already sufficiently debated but requiring factual elucidation.
2. Defiance of a party Whip can attract disqualification under the Sixth Schedule.
3. The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are not binding on the executive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: a half-an-hour discussion is held on a matter sufficiently debated that needs further factual elucidation.
Statement 2: Incorrect: defiance of the Whip can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, not the Sixth.
Statement 3: Correct: PAC recommendations are not binding on the executive.

43.s: Which of the following pairs of cut motions is correctly matched?
o: Policy cut – Reduction of the demand by Rs 100
Token cut – Reduction of the demand to Re 1
Economy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
Policy cut – Reduction by a specified amount
43.x: An economy cut reduces the demand by a specified amount; a policy cut reduces it to Re 1 and a token cut by Rs 100.
xa: Cut motions are moved on **demands for grants** in the **Lok Sabha**.
**Budget approval** is one of the listed tools of parliamentary control.
The **Estimates Committee** suggests economies and efficiency in the estimates.

43.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Simple closure — Only important clauses are debated
Closure by compartments — All pending clauses are voted on when time ends
Kangaroo closure — Only important clauses are debated and the others are taken as passed
Guillotine — Matter is declared sufficiently discussed and put to vote
43.x: C is correct: under kangaroo closure only the important clauses are debated and the rest are taken as passed. A is wrong because simple closure means the matter is declared sufficiently discussed and put to vote; B is wrong because putting all pending clauses to vote when time ends is the guillotine; D is wrong because it describes simple closure, not the guillotine.
43.tq: Discriminate among similar closure terms by matching each device with its exact operation.
xs: **Kangaroo closure — only important clauses debated, others taken as passed** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Simple closure** = matter sufficiently discussed, put to vote; **closure by compartments** = clauses grouped into parts, debated and voted part by part.
Voting all pending clauses when time ends is the **guillotine**, not simple closure.
xa: ⚠ Kangaroo = only important clauses debated; guillotine = **undiscussed** clauses voted when allotted time ends.
**Point of order**: raised when proceedings depart from rules; no debate.
Whips: **one-line** informative, **two-line** attendance, **three-line** strict voting.

43.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Two-line Whip – Direction to attend the House
One-line Whip – Direction to attend the House
43.x: A two-line Whip directs members to attend; a one-line Whip is informative and a three-line Whip gives a strict voting direction.
xa: Defying the whip on a vote can attract **Tenth Schedule** disqualification.
The office of Whip rests on **conventions** of parliamentary government.
Each party appoints a **whip / chief whip**.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about legislative devices and committees:
1. The form of closure in which all remaining clauses or demands are put to vote at once when the allotted time expires is called the guillotine.
2. The no-confidence motion carried against the Prakasam ministry of Andhra State in November 1954 was moved by Gouthu Latchanna.
3. Consultative Committees of MPs for particular ministries are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: the guillotine puts all remaining clauses or demands to vote at once when the allotted time runs out.
Statement 2: Correct: Gouthu Latchanna's motion was carried by 69 votes to 68 in November 1954, and the Prakasam ministry fell.
Statement 3: Correct: Consultative Committees are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.

43.s:
Consider the following statements about a no-confidence motion:
1. Reasons for moving it must be stated.
2. The Speaker decides whether to admit it.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
43.x: The Speaker has discretion to admit or reject a no-confidence motion; reasons need not be stated, and it can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the Speaker does **not resign or dissolve** the House.
It is the **most powerful weapon** of executive accountability (APPSC-G2 2025).
⚠ "Reasons must be stated" = **censure motion**.

43.s: The daily listing of Short Notice Questions is at the discretion of whom?
o: The Leader of the House only
43.x: Short notice questions are listed each day at the discretion of the Speaker or Chairman, who decides whether the matter is urgent enough.
43.tq: Recall who admits short notice questions.
n: The daily listing of Short Notice Questions is at the discretion of the Speaker or Chairman. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
xs: Short Notice listing is at the discretion of the **Speaker or Chairman** — option **(4)**.
Such questions concern **urgent** public importance with notice shorter than **10 clear days**.
They receive an **oral** answer; **supplementaries** are allowed.
xa: Starred: at most **20** per day; unstarred: no such limit.
Short notice paper colour: **light pink**.
All three types are taken up in **Question Hour**.

43.s: Which of the following is not a tool of Legislative control over the administration in India?
Which one of the following motions, the Council of Ministers in India can move?
43.x: The Council of Ministers in India can move ‘’Confidence Motion’’. A Motion of 'No Confidence' can be introduced only in Lok Sabha (the Lower House of the Parliament). The Government brings the ‘Motion of Confidence’ in Lok Sabha when it has to prove the confidence or support of a majority in the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

43.s:
Consider the following statements about control over the executive:
1. Judicial review by the Supreme Court is not included among the recognised tools of parliamentary control over the executive.
2. The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table primarily checks whether public sector undertakings follow commercial principles.
3. The reform area associated with the Ashok Dalwai Committee includes value addition and land leasing in the context of doubling farmers' income.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
43.x:
Statement 1: Correct: judicial review is a constitutional function of the judiciary, not a parliamentary device.
Statement 2: Incorrect: the Committee checks whether papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, comply with the relevant requirements.
Statement 3: Correct: Ashok Dalwai's reform area concerns doubling farmers' income, including value addition and land leasing.

43.s: What could be the maximum time limit of “Zero Hour” in the Lok Sabha?
In which of the following hours, members of the Parliament are free to raise any matter that they think is important? 296
43.x: " Zero Hour " is an informal parliamentary practice occurring after Question Hour, allowing MPs to raise urgent matters without prior notice. Question Hour, by contrast, is formally structured for presubmitted questions to ministers, distinguishing it from Zero Hour's spontaneous character.

43.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of questions asked by the Members in the Parliament of India:
1. Unstarred questions are those to which a Member desires an oral answer in the House.
2. Starred questions are those to which a Member desires a written answer.
3. No supplementary question can be asked on an unstarred question. Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
o: All the three statements are correct.
There are two correct statements, that include statement 2.
There is only one correct statement.
43.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: Unstarred Questions require a written answer, not an oral answer. A Starred Question is the one that requires an oral answer. Statement 2 is incorrect: Starred Questions require an oral answer, not a written one. Statement 3 is correct: Since Unstarred Questions are answered in writing, no supplementary question can be asked on them.

43.s:
Statement(A) : N.D.A. Government does not like discussion under Rule 184 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha.
Reason(R) : This Rule provides for voting also along with discussion.
Select the correct answer using :
o: (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation
(A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not correct explanation
43.x: Both, the statement (A) and Reason (R), are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). According to Rule 184, after a discussion on a matter, voting shall take place, if the ruling Party gets fewer votes in its favour, then it may lose the ruling position.

43.s: Under Rule 377 of Rules and Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the maximum number of matters that can be raised by Lok Sabha members in one day are
43.x: Closure Motion - A motion moved by a member to cut short the debate on a matter before the House. There are four kinds of Closure Motions, Guillotine is one of them. In the Guillotine, the undiscussed clauses of a bill or a resolution are also put to vote along with the discussed ones due to a lack of time (as the time allotted for the discussion is over)

43.s: In the Parliament of India, the purpose of an Adjournment Motion is:
o: to allow a discussion on a definite matter of urgent public importance
to let opposition members, collect information from the ministers
to allow a reduction of specific amount in demand for grant
to postpone the proceedings to check the inappropriate or violent behaviour on the part of some members
43.x: Indian Polity: Organs of the State PMF IAS IP – 75 An Adjournment Motion is a parliamentary device used in the Lok Sabha to draw the attention of the House to a definite matter of urgent public importance. For the motion to be admitted, it must be supported by at least 50 members. Since it interrupts the normal business of the House, it is considered an extraordinary parliamentary device. The motion also carries an element of censure against the government, which is why it is not permitted in the Rajya Sabha. The discussion on an adjournment motion should last for not less than two hours and thirty minutes.

o: To allow a discussion on a definite matter of urgent
To let opposition members collect information from

42.x: Statement 1 is correct: Ordinary Bills and certain Financial Bills require agreement from both Houses of Parliament for passage, meaning the Rajya Sabha can reject or amend them. While the Rajya Sabha cannot alter Money Bills (Art. 110), it has equal power over Ordinary and Financial Bills, with deadlocks resolvable through joint sittings. Statement 2 is correct: The role of the Rajya Sabha in passing Money Bills is restricted. Such Bills can originate only in the Lok Sabha. Once a Money Bill is passed by the Lok Sabha, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations. The Rajya Sabha must return the Bill within 14 days, along with its non-binding suggestions. If the Lok Sabha rejects these recommendations, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses in the original form Indian Polity: Organs of the State PMF IAS IP – 60 approved by the Lok Sabha. Even if the Rajya Sabha fails to return the Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed passed in the same manner. Therefore, in the case of Money Bills, the Rajya Sabha holds only an advisory role. Statement 3 is incorrect: The President can summon (does not become necessary) a joint sitting of both Houses to resolve differences over a deadlock. There is no provision for a joint sitting for differences over a Money Bill.

With reference to Finance Bill and Money Bill in the Indian Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. When the Lok Sabha transmits Finance Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it can amend or reject the Bill.
2. When the Lok Sabha transmits Money Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it cannot amend or reject the Bill, it can only make recommendations.
3. In the case of disagreement between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, there is no joint sitting for Money Bill, but a joint sitting becomes necessary for Finance Bill.
How many of the above statements are correct?
42.x: Financial bills, in a technical sense, are those bills that deal with fiscal matters, that is, revenue or expenditure, and are generally of three kinds: 1. Money bills-Article 110, 2. Financial bills (I)-Article 117 (1), 3. Financial bills (II)-Article 117 (3). But the Constitution, under Article 109, provides a special procedure in respect of Money Bills and Article 110 defines the "Money Bills". The Rajya Sabha has restricted powers regarding a money bill. It cannot reject or amend a money bill. It can only make the recommendations and it must return the bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days, whether with or without recommendations. A financial bill (I) is similar to a money bill in two respects. Both of them can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha, and both of them can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President. In all other respects, a financial bill (I) is governed by the same legislative procedure applicable to an ordinary bill. Hence, it can be either rejected or amended by the Rajya Sabha. Hence statement 1 and statement 2 are correct. No joint sitting of the two houses is allowed with regard to a money bill under Article 108. However Financial bills (I) and Financial bills (II) are governed by the same legislative procedure applicable to an ordinary bill, the President may (not necessarily) summon a joint sitting of the two Houses to resolve the deadlock. Hence, statement 3 is not correct.
